%-----------------------------------------------
\subsection{Delimiters and their sizes}

\sourcefile{ltmath,fontdef}
\begin{function}[user]
  {
    \big,
    \bigg
  }
  \begin{syntax}
    \cs{big} \meta{delimiter}
  \end{syntax}
  Typeset \meta{delimiter} in a fixed larger size (\cs{Big} and
  \cs{Bigg} are even larger). Unlike \cs{left} and \cs{right} the
  size doesn't depend on the enclosed material and the delimiters
  need not come in pairs. These forms produce an ordinary symbol,
  i.e., without the spacing of the variants below.
\end{function}
\modifiedby[big]{a0size, breqn, ccfonts, delimset, eulervm, mathpazo,
  mathpple, mathptm, mathptmx, mdwmath, sexscale, stix, stix2}
\modifiedby[bigg]{a0size, breqn, ccfonts, delimset, eulervm, fdsymbol,
  mathpazo, mathpple, mathptm, mathptmx, mdwmath, sexscale}



\sourcefile{ltmath}
\begin{function}[user]
  {
    \bigl,
    \bigm,
    \bigr
  }
  \begin{syntax}
    \cs{bigl} \meta{delimiter} \ldots \cs{bigr} \meta{delimiter}
  \end{syntax}
  Like \cs{big} but the delimiter becomes an opening symbol
  (\cs{bigl}), a relation (\cs{bigm}, e.g., for a middle bar), or a
  closing symbol (\cs{bigr}), so that the spacing is correct.
\end{function}
\modifiedby[bigl]{breqn, nath}
\modifiedby[bigm]{nath}
\modifiedby[bigr]{breqn, nath}



\sourcefile{ltmath}
\begin{function}[user]
  {
    \biggl,
    \biggm,
    \biggr
  }
  \begin{syntax}
    \cs{biggl} \meta{delimiter} \ldots \cs{biggr} \meta{delimiter}
  \end{syntax}
  As \cs{bigl}, \cs{bigm}, and \cs{bigr}, but in the size of \cs{bigg}.
\end{function}
\modifiedby[biggl]{breqn, nath}
\modifiedby[biggm]{nath}
\modifiedby[biggr]{breqn, nath}

\begin{function}[]

\subsection{Math internals}

\sourcefile{ltfssbas}
\begin{function}[]
  {
    \everymath,
    \everydisplay
  }
  \begin{syntax}
    \cs{everymath}=\Arg{code}
  \end{syntax}
  These are no longer the \TeX{} primitives but token registers that
  are executed from \cs{frozen@everymath} and
  \cs{frozen@everydisplay}, respectively (after \LaTeX{} has done what
  it wants to do to set up math). Packages may add code to them.

  This is not the engine primitive \cs{everymath} but a \LaTeX{} command
  replacing it; the original primitive is still available as
  \cs{frozen@everymath} but not to be used.
  This is not the engine primitive \cs{everydisplay} but a \LaTeX{} command
  replacing it; the original primitive is still available as
  \cs{frozen@everydisplay} but not to be used.
\end{function}
\modifiedby[everymath]{}
\modifiedby[everydisplay]{}

%-----------------------------------------------
\subsection{The \env{document} environment}

\sourcefile{ltfiles,ltmiscen}
\begin{function}[user]
  {
    \document,
    \enddocument
  }
  \begin{syntax}
    \cs{begin}\Arg{document}  \meta{document body} \cs{end}\Arg{document}
  \end{syntax}
  The \env{document} environment. \cs{begin}\texttt{\{document\}}
  ends the preamble: it reads the \texttt{.aux} file, runs the
  \texttt{begindocument} hooks, and disables preamble-only commands.
  \cs{end}\texttt{\{document\}} outputs the remaining material, runs
  the \texttt{enddocument} hooks, writes and checks the \texttt{.aux}
  file (e.g., for changed labels), and ends the run.
\end{function}

\sourcefile{ltsect}
\begin{variable}[readonly]
  {
    \@contentsline@destination
  }
  The link destination (fourth argument) of the \cs{contentsline}
  being processed, for use by the \cs{l@\meta{type}} commands.
\end{variable}
\modifiedby{etoc}
\publicusedby{ltugboat, ltx-talk, sblbook, sblreport, tocloft}



\begin{function}[settable]
  {
    \l@\meta{type}
  }
  \begin{syntax}
    \cs{l@\meta{type}} \Arg{entry} \Arg{page}
  \end{syntax}
  Typesets an entry of type \meta{type} in a contents list (table of
  contents, list of figures, \ldots), where \meta{type} is the second
  argument of \cs{addcontentsline}: a sectioning level (\cs{l@section})
  or a float type (\cs{l@figure}). Defined by the classes, usually with
  \cs{@dottedtocline}. Note that babel and \cs{newlanguage} use names of
  the same form, \cs{l@}\meta{language}, for language numbers.
  \meta{type} may contain characters other than letters; then the
  command can only be used via \cs{csname} \ldots{} \cs{endcsname} (or
  \cs{@nameuse}, \cs{@namedef}, \ldots).
\end{function}



\begin{variable}[int,readonly]
  {
    \tf@\meta{ext}
  }
  The write stream of the contents file \cs{jobname}\texttt{.}\meta{ext}
  (\texttt{toc}, \texttt{lof}, \texttt{lot}, \ldots), allocated and
  opened by \cs{@starttoc}\Arg{ext} unless \cs{nofiles} is in effect;
  \cs{@writefile} writes to it. \meta{ext} may contain characters other
  than letters; then the command can only be used via \cs{csname}
  \ldots{} \cs{endcsname} (or \cs{@nameuse}, \cs{@namedef}, \ldots).
\end{variable}

\subsection{Lists}

\sourcefile{ltlists}
\begin{function}[]
  {
    \list,
    \endlist
  }
  \begin{syntax}
    \cs{begin}\Arg{list}\Arg{default-label}\Arg{declarations}  \cs{item} ... \cs{end}\Arg{list}
  \end{syntax}
  The generic list environment on which \env{itemize},
  \env{enumerate}, \env{quote}, etc.\ are built.
  \meta{default-label} is used for \cs{item} without optional argument;
  \meta{declarations} set the list parameters (\cs{leftmargin},
  \cs{itemsep}, etc.) and typically \cs{usecounter}. Normally used
  inside the definition of other environments.
\end{function}

\begin{variable}[settable]
  {
    \topsep,
    \partopsep,
    \itemsep,
    \parsep
  }
  Vertical spacing of lists: \cs{topsep} is added above and below
  the list (plus \cs{partopsep} if the list starts a new paragraph),
  \cs{itemsep} between items, and \cs{parsep} between paragraphs within
  an item. Usually set in the \meta{declarations} of \env{list} or
  in \cs[no-index]{@list\meta{level}} by the class.
\end{variable}

\begin{function}[user,settable]
  {
    \itemize,
    \enditemize
  }
  \begin{syntax}
    \cs{begin}\texttt{\{itemize\}} \cs{item} \ldots{} \cs{end}\texttt{\{itemize\}}
  \end{syntax}
  The commands behind the \env{itemize} environment: a list whose items
  are marked with \cs{labelitemi}, \cs{labelitemii}, \ldots{} depending
  on the nesting level (at most four levels). Classes and packages may
  redefine them to change the layout of such lists.
\end{function}

\begin{function}[user,settable]
  {

    \endenumerate
  }
  \begin{syntax}
    \cs{begin}\texttt{\{enumerate\}} \cs{item} \ldots{} \cs{end}\texttt{\{enumerate\}}
  \end{syntax}
  The commands behind the \env{enumerate} environment: a list whose
  items are numbered with the counters \texttt{enumi}, \texttt{enumii},
  \ldots{} depending on the nesting level (at most four levels), using
  \cs{labelenumi} etc.\ for the labels. Classes and packages may
  redefine them to change the layout of such lists.
\end{function}

\sourcefile{ltlists}
\begin{function}[]
  {
    \trivlist,
    \endtrivlist
  }
  \begin{syntax}
    \cs{begin}\texttt{\{trivlist\}} \cs{item}\oarg{label} \ldots{} \cs{end}\texttt{\{trivlist\}}
  \end{syntax}
  A restricted form of \env{list} without margins, label width or
  item indentation (\cs{leftmargin}, \cs{labelwidth} and
  \cs{itemindent} are zero) and with \cs{parsep} set to
  \cs{parskip}. It is the basis of many list-like environments, e.g.,
  \env{center}, \env{verbatim} and theorems, which typically
  contain a single \cs{item} that does not produce any visible output.

  For accessible documents this is a bad practice because none of the
  use cases are really lists so should not pretend they are just for
  visial reasons. Going forward, \LaTeX{} therefore starts to replace
  \env{trivlist} altogether and when \cs{DocumentMetadata} is used
  none of the above environments make use of a list structure
  internally.
\end{function}

  smfbook}
\modifiedby[endtrivlist]{beamerbaseoverlay, powerdot}

\sourcefile{ltlists}
\begin{function}[user]
  {
    \usecounter
  }
  \begin{syntax}
    \cs{usecounter} \Arg{counter}
  \end{syntax}
  Used in the second argument of \cs{list} to number the items with
  \meta{counter}: it resets \meta{counter} to zero and makes \cs{item}
  step it (with \cs{refstepcounter}, so the item can be referenced).
\end{function}
\modifiedby{multibib}

\begin{variable}[int]
  {
    \@outerparskip
  }
  Skip register: the value of \cs{parskip} outside the current list,
  saved by \cs{list} to add the right amount of space before an item
  that starts a new paragraph.
\end{variable}

\begin{variable}[]
  {
    \@enumdepth,
    \@itemdepth
  }
  Count registers: the nesting depth of the \env{enumerate} and
  \env{itemize} environments (0 outside), used to select the
  counter and label for the current level and to issue the
  \enquote{Too deeply nested} error after four levels.
\end{variable}

\begin{function}[user,settable]
  {
    \labelitem\meta{level}
  }
  \begin{syntax}
    \cs{labelitem\meta{level}}
  \end{syntax}
  The label of the items of an \env{itemize} list at nesting level
  \meta{level} (\texttt{i}, \texttt{ii}, \texttt{iii} or \texttt{iv}),
  i.e., \cs{labelitemi} to \cs{labelitemiv}; defined by the classes
  and redefined to change the bullets.
\end{function}



\begin{function}[user,settable]
  {
    \labelenum\meta{level}
  }
  \begin{syntax}
    \cs{labelenum\meta{level}}
  \end{syntax}
  The label of the items of an \env{enumerate} list at nesting level
  \meta{level} (\texttt{i} to \texttt{iv}), i.e., \cs{labelenumi} to
  \cs{labelenumiv}; defined by the classes in terms of the counters
  \texttt{enum}\meta{level}. These are ordinary counters, i.e.,
  \cs{theenumi}, \cs{p@enumii}, \ldots{} follow the scheme of
  \cs{the\meta{counter}} and \cs{p@\meta{counter}}.
\end{function}



\begin{variable}[settable]
  {
    \leftmargin\meta{level}
  }
  Dimen registers: the left margin of a list at nesting level
  \meta{level} (\texttt{i} to \texttt{vi}), i.e., \cs{leftmargini} to
  \cs{leftmarginvi}. The \cs{list} environment sets \cs{leftmargin} to
  the value for the current level before executing \cs{@list\meta{level}}
  and its second argument. Set by the classes.
\end{variable}



\begin{function}[settable]
  {
    \@list\meta{level}
  }
  \begin{syntax}
    \cs{@list\meta{level}}
  \end{syntax}
  The parameter settings of a list at nesting level \meta{level}
  (\texttt{i} to \texttt{vi}), i.e., \cs{@listi} to \cs{@listvi},
  executed by \cs{list}: typically they set \cs{leftmargin},
  \cs{topsep}, \cs{parsep}, \cs{itemsep} etc. Defined by the
  classes; \cs{@listi} is also redefined by the size commands
  (\cs{small}, \cs{footnotesize}, \ldots).
\end{function}

\subsection{Labels and references}

\sourcefile{ltxref}
\begin{function}[user]
  {
    \refstepcounter
  }
  \begin{syntax}
    \cs{refstepcounter} \Arg{name}
  \end{syntax}
  Like \cs{stepcounter}, but in addition makes \meta{name} the current
  counter (\cs{@currentcounter}), sets \cs{@currentlabel} to
  \cs{p@\meta{name}}\cs{the\meta{name}} so that a following \cs{label}
  refers to it, and sets a link target (used by \pkg{hyperref} and
  tagging) via the socket \texttt{refstepcounter/target}.
\end{function}

  crossreference, cwebbase.tex, datatool-base, floatrow, fncylab,
  glossaries, glossaries-2022-11-03, glossaries-2024-04-03,
  glossaries-2025-03-19, hyper, hyperref, locality, ltcaption, relabel,
  scrartcl, scrartcl-xetex-bidi.def, scrbook, scrbook-xetex-bidi.def,
  scrreprt, scrreprt-xetex-bidi.def, showexpl, subfig, xassoccnt,
  zref-counter}



\sourcefile{ltxref}
\begin{function}[]
  {
    \@kernel@refstepcounter
  }
  \begin{syntax}
    \cs{@kernel@refstepcounter} \Arg{name}
  \end{syntax}
  A version of \cs{refstepcounter} that does not set a link target.
  Used by the kernel where the target is created separately.
\end{function}

\begin{variable}[settable]
  {
    \@currentlabel
  }
  The text that a \cs{label} command writes to the \texttt{.aux} file,
  i.e., what a later \cs{ref} produces. Normally set by
  \cs{refstepcounter}, but code may set it directly (with
  \cs{protected@edef}) to make \cs{label} refer to something else.
\end{variable}

  hyperref and others with further fields; used by \cs{ref} and

  \cs{csname} \ldots{} \cs{endcsname} (or \cs{@nameuse}, \cs{@namedef},
  \ldots).

\begin{variable}[int,readonly]
  {
    \@floatpenalty
  }
  Count register: the state of the float or marginal note being
  processed, set at its start: $-10002$ if started in horizontal mode,
  $-10003$ if started in vertical mode, and $0$ if it cannot be placed
  (inside a box or minipage, or no float boxes left). Used at its end
  to decide how to pass it to the output routine.
\end{variable}

\sourcefile{ltfloat}
\begin{function}[int]
  {
    \@float,
    \@xfloat
  }
  \begin{syntax}
    \cs{@float} \Arg{type} \oarg{placement}
  \end{syntax}
  Start of a single-column float environment of type \meta{type},
  e.g., \cs{figure} is \cs{@float}\texttt{\{figure\}}. Without
  \meta{placement} the default \cs{fps@}\meta{type} is used.
  \cs{@xfloat} does the work: it sets \cs{@captype} and \cs{@fps},
  takes a box from \cs{@freelist} and starts the float box. Ended by
  \cs{end@float}.
\end{function}

\sourcefile{ltfloat}
\begin{function}[int]
  {
    \@dblfloat,
    \@dbflt,
    \@xdblfloat
  }
  \begin{syntax}
    \cs{@dblfloat} \Arg{type} \oarg{placement}
  \end{syntax}
  Start of a double-column float environment (e.g.,
  \env{figure*}). In one-column mode it is the same as \cs{@float};
  in two-column mode \cs{@dbflt} and \cs{@xdblfloat} start a float of
  width \cs{textwidth} with the default placement \texttt{tp}. Ended by
  \cs{end@dblfloat}.
\end{function}

\begin{function}[int]

    \cs{@setnobreak}
  \end{syntax}

\begin{variable}[settable]
  {
    \ext@\meta{float}
  }
  The extension of the contents file that lists the floats of type
  \meta{float}, e.g., \texttt{lof} for \cs{ext@figure}, \texttt{lot} for
  \cs{ext@table}; used by \cs{@caption} for \cs{addcontentsline}.
  Defined by the classes for every float type. \meta{float} may contain
  characters other than letters; then the command can only be used via
  \cs{csname} \ldots{} \cs{endcsname} (or \cs{@nameuse}, \cs{@namedef},
  \ldots).
\end{variable}



\begin{variable}[settable]
  {
    \fps@\meta{float}
  }
  The default placement specifier of floats of type \meta{float}, used
  if the float environment has no optional argument (e.g.,
  \texttt{tbp}). Defined by the classes for every float type.
  \meta{float} may contain characters other than letters; then the
  command can only be used via \cs{csname} \ldots{} \cs{endcsname} (or
  \cs{@nameuse}, \cs{@namedef}, \ldots).
\end{variable}



\begin{variable}[readonly]
  {
    \ftype@\meta{float}
  }
  The type number of floats of type \meta{float}: a different power of 2
  for each type (1 for \texttt{figure}, 2 for \texttt{table}); floats of
  the same type are kept in order. Defined by the classes for every
  float type. \meta{float} may contain characters other than letters;
  then the command can only be used via \cs{csname} \ldots{}
  \cs{endcsname} (or \cs{@nameuse}, \cs{@namedef}, \ldots).
\end{variable}



\begin{variable}[int,readonly]
  {
    \bx@\meta{id}
  }
  The insertions (i.e., box registers with associated registers)
  available for floats and marginal notes, kept in \cs{@freelist}: the
  kernel allocates 52 (\cs{bx@A} to \cs{bx@Z} and \cs{bx@AA} to
  \cs{bx@ZZ}), \cs{extrafloats} adds more, named \cs{bx@\meta{number}}.
  The names \cs{bx@A} to \cs{bx@ZZ} consist of letters; for those
  allocated by \cs{extrafloats}, which contain digits, the command can
  only be used via \cs{csname} \ldots{} \cs{endcsname} (or
  \cs{@nameuse}, \cs{@namedef}, \ldots).
\end{variable}

\sourcefile{ltfloat}
\begin{function}[user]
  {
    \caption
  }
  \begin{syntax}
    \cs{caption} \oarg{short text} \Arg{text}
  \end{syntax}
  Inside a float environment: steps the counter of the float type
  (\cs{@captype}) with \cs{refstepcounter}, so a following \cs{label}
  refers to it, and typesets the caption with \cs{@caption}. The
  \meta{short text} (default \meta{text}) goes into the list of figures,
  tables, etc. Outside a float an error is issued.
\end{function}

\sourcefile{ltfloat}
\begin{function}[settable]
  {
    \@caption
  }
  \begin{syntax}
    \cs{@caption} \Arg{type} \oarg{short text} \Arg{text}
  \end{syntax}
  Called by \cs{caption} with the float type: writes the entry for the
  list of figures (\cs{ext@}\meta{type}) and typesets the caption with
  \cs{@makecaption}, using \cs{fnum@}\meta{type} as the label, with
  the paragraph parameters reset and in \cs{normalsize}. Redefined by
  many packages that change the layout of captions.

  In accessessible documents (\cs{DocumentMetadata} this interface
  will most likely be deprecated.
\end{function}

\sourcefile{ltfloat}
\begin{function}[user]
  {
    \footnotemark
  }
  \begin{syntax}
    \cs{footnotemark} \oarg{number}
  \end{syntax}
  Typesets a footnote mark without the footnote text. Without the
  optional argument it steps the \texttt{footnote} counter; with
  \meta{number} it uses that number and leaves the counter unchanged.
  The text is then given with \cs{footnotetext}.
\end{function}

\sourcefile{ltfloat}
\begin{function}[user]
  {
    \footnotetext
  }
  \begin{syntax}
    \cs{footnotetext} \oarg{number} \Arg{text}
  \end{syntax}
  Typesets a footnote text without a mark in the running text, using
  the current value of the footnote counter (or \meta{number}) for the
  mark in front of \meta{text}. The counter is not stepped. Inside a
  \env{minipage} it uses the \texttt{mpfootnote} counter.
\end{function}

  {
    \footref

    \cs{footref} \Arg{label}
  \end{syntax}

\subsection{Marginal notes}



\sourcefile{ltfloat}
\begin{function}[user]
  {
    \marginpar
  }
  \begin{syntax}
    \cs{marginpar} \oarg{left text} \Arg{text}
  \end{syntax}
  Places \meta{text} as a marginal note next to the current line. If
  \meta{left text} is given, it is used instead when the note goes into
  the left margin. Marginal notes are handled like floats and use up a
  float box; they are not allowed in inner mode (boxes, minipages,
  floats).
\end{function}
\modifiedby{arabtex.tex, beamerfoils, bgteubner, cje, classicthesis,
  csquotes, lwarp, marginfit, marginfix, minipage-marginpar, mnotes,
  mw10.clo, mw11.clo, mw12.clo, mwbk10.clo, mwbk11.clo, mwbk12.clo,
  paracol, paracol-2018-12-31, refart, refrep, rgltxdoc, seminar,
  showexpl, sidenotesplus, suftesi, tudscrdoc, tudscrmanual, uiucthesis,
  xsim-manual, ycbook}



\sourcefile{ltfloat}
\begin{function}[user]
  {
    \reversemarginpar,
    \normalmarginpar
  }
  \begin{syntax}
    \cs{reversemarginpar}
    \cs{normalmarginpar}
  \end{syntax}
  Declarations: \cs{reversemarginpar} puts the following marginal notes
  into the opposite margin from the default one (e.g., into the left
  margin in one-column documents); \cs{normalmarginpar} returns to the
  default.
\end{function}
\modifiedby[reversemarginpar]{lwarp}
\modifiedby[normalmarginpar]{lwarp}



\sourcefile{ltfloat}
\begin{function}[]
  {
    \@marginparreset
  }
  \begin{syntax}
    \cs{@marginparreset}
  \end{syntax}
  Executed at the start of every marginal note: resets the font
  (\cs{reset@font}), selects \cs{normalsize} and calls
  \cs{@setminipage}.
\end{function}
\modifiedby{babelbidi-api-layout.def, exam-n, sapthesis, unifith}
\publicusedby{}



\sourcefile{ltfloat}
\begin{function}[int]
  {
    \@xmpar,
    \@ympar,
    \@xympar
  }
  \begin{syntax}
    \cs{@xmpar} \oarg{left text} \Arg{text}
    \cs{@ympar} \Arg{text}
  \end{syntax}
  Implementation of \cs{marginpar} with and without optional argument:
  they put the left and right versions of the note into \cs{@marbox}
  and \cs{@currbox}; \cs{@xympar} then passes them to the output
  routine.
\end{function}

  latex-xetex-bidi.def, mparhack, sapthesis, unifith}

  paracol-2018-12-31, reledmac, textpos}

\usedby[@ympar]{}
\usedby[@xympar]{bidituftesidenote, caesar\_book, latex-xetex-bidi.def,
  mparhack, sapthesis, unifith}



\sourcefile{ltfloat}
\begin{function}[int]
  {
    \@savemarbox
  }
  \begin{syntax}
    \cs{@savemarbox} \meta{box} \Arg{text}
  \end{syntax}
  Sets \meta{text} globally into \meta{box} as a \cs{vtop} of width
  \cs{marginparwidth}, with the paragraph parameters reset and
  \cs{@marginparreset} applied.
\end{function}
\modifiedby{}

\begin{function}[settable]
  {
    \\meta{section}mark
  }
  \begin{syntax}
    \cs{\meta{section}mark} \Arg{title}
  \end{syntax}
  Called by the sectioning command \meta{section} (\cs{chapter},
  \cs{section}, \ldots) with the (short) title, to set the marks for the
  running heads. Does nothing by default; page styles such as
  \texttt{headings} and \texttt{myheadings} redefine the ones they need,
  e.g., \cs{sectionmark} to call \cs{markright}. \meta{section} may
  contain characters other than letters; then the command can only be
  used via \cs{csname} \ldots{} \cs{endcsname} (or \cs{@nameuse},
  \cs{@namedef}, \ldots).
\end{function}



\begin{function}[settable]
  {
    \ps@\meta{style}
  }
  \begin{syntax}
    \cs{ps@\meta{style}}
  \end{syntax}
  Sets up the page style \meta{style}, i.e., defines \cs{@oddhead},
  \cs{@oddfoot}, \cs{@evenhead}, \cs{@evenfoot} and the
  \cs{\meta{section}mark} commands; executed by
  \cs{pagestyle}\Arg{style} and \cs{thispagestyle}\Arg{style}. Defining
  such a command creates a new page style. \meta{style} may contain
  characters other than letters; then the command can only be used via
  \cs{csname} \ldots{} \cs{endcsname} (or \cs{@nameuse}, \cs{@namedef},
  \ldots).
\end{function}

\section{Tagging and accessibility}


%-----------------------------------------------
\subsection{Tagging support}

The commands below are always available, so packages can use them
whether or not tagging is active; without tagging most do nothing.



\sourcefile{lttagging}
\begin{function}[]
  {
    \SuspendTagging,
    \ResumeTagging
  }
  \begin{syntax}
    \cs{SuspendTagging}\Arg{label} \meta{material} \cs{ResumeTagging}\Arg{label}
  \end{syntax}
  Stop (and restart) tagging, e.g., around trial typesetting that is
  done several times or thrown away (as in measuring with
  \cs{settowidth}). The \meta{label} is only used in debugging
  messages and is not expanded.
\end{function}

  sillypage, tabulary, tocloft, xltabular}

    \NewTaggingSocketPlug,

\begin{function}[]
  {
    \UseTaggingSocket,
    \UseExpandableTaggingSocket
  }
  \begin{syntax}
    \cs{UseTaggingSocket} \Arg{name} \meta{inputs}
  \end{syntax}
  Like \cs{UseSocket} for \texttt{tagsupport/\meta{name}}, but if
  tagging is suspended or not active the socket is bypassed: with no
  input nothing happens, with one input the input is returned
  unchanged. The expandable variant can be used in expansion contexts
  (with plugs that are expandable).
\end{function}

\subsection{Unicode data and engine set-up}

During format generation the kernel reads the Unicode data files to
set up character codes (catcodes, case mappings, etc.). The commands
below are used only for that.



\begin{constant}
  {
    \eTeXversion,
    \luatexversion,
    \XeTeXversion
  }
  Return the version number of e-\TeX{},
  Lua\TeX{}, or Xe\TeX{}. They are undefined in other engines, so
  their existence can be used to detect the engine, e.g.,
  \cs{ifdefined}\cs{luatexversion}. For new code the L3 programming
  layer tests such as \texttt{\textbackslash sys\_if\_engine\_luatex:TF}
  are preferable.

  \cs{eTeXversion} is an engine primitive.
  \cs{luatexversion} is an engine primitive (Lua\TeX{} only).
  \cs{XeTeXversion} is an engine primitive (Xe\TeX{} only).
\end{constant}

%===============================================
\section{Compatibility and deprecated commands}


%-----------------------------------------------
\subsection{Plain \TeX{} leftovers}

\LaTeX\,2.09 started out as a format on top of plain \TeX{} and kept a
number of plain \TeX{} commands. Some of them have been useful in
programming \LaTeXe{} macros, though the L3 programming layer provides
much better alternatives.  A few ended up in regular use in user
documents, but with a few exceptions this is not recommended!



\sourcefile{ltboxes}
\begin{function}[user]
  {
    \centerline,
    \leftline,
    \rightline
  }
  \begin{syntax}
    \cs{centerline} \Arg{material}
  \end{syntax}
  %
  Produces a \cs{hbox} of size \cs{hsize} and typesets the
  \meta{material} inside, either centered, flush left, or flush
  right. As a simple \cs{hbox} it does not start a paragraph (as
  \cs{mbox} or \cs{makebox} do), and in a list it ignores the
  indentation.

\end{function}
\modifiedby[centerline]{klufloa, kluwer, latex-xetex-bidi.def, lwarp,
  plain-xetex-bidi.def}
\modifiedby[leftline]{latex-xetex-bidi.def, lwarp, plain-xetex-bidi.def}
\modifiedby[rightline]{latex-xetex-bidi.def, lwarp,
  plain-xetex-bidi.def}



\sourcefile{ltboxes}
\begin{function}[int, deprecated]
  {
    \@@line
  }
  \begin{syntax}
    \cs{@@line} \Arg{material}
  \end{syntax}
  Command to implement \cs{centerline}, \cs{leftline}, and
  \cs{rightline}.  Deprecated, do not use directly.
\end{function}
\modifiedby{euproposal, memoir}
\usedby{csbulletin, csbulobalka, dvipaste, eledmac, examdesign,
  extrafootnotefeatures-xetex-bidi.def, latex-xetex-bidi.def, ledmac,
  plain, proposal, reledmac, rotating-xetex-bidi.def, truncate}



\sourcefile{ltboxes}
\begin{function}[]
  {
    \clap,
    \llap,
    \rlap
  }
  \begin{syntax}
    \cs{rlap} \Arg{material}
  \end{syntax}
  %
  Puts the \meta{material} into an \cs{hbox} of zero width together
  with \cs{hss} on one or both sides. As a result, the material sticks
  out of the box without taking up any size in \LaTeX{}'s eyes. Thus
  one can overprint material or have something sticking out into the
  margin, etc. However, as this is using an \cs{hbox} no paragraph is
  started so if this command is used just in front of a paragraph it
  will appear on a line before the paragraph---not where most people
  would expect it.

  The safer \LaTeX{} equivalent would be
  \cs{makebox}\oarg{position}\texttt{\{0pt\}}\Arg{material} as this would
  always start a paragraph, if necessary.
\end{function}

\subsection{Deprecated kernel commands}



\sourcefile{ltclass}
\begin{function}[int, deprecated]
  {
    \@begindocumenthook
  }
  \begin{syntax}
    \cs{@begindocumenthook}
  
  \todo[inline]{Needs checking (settable review).}
\end{syntax}
  The \LaTeXe{} hook for code to run at \verb|\begin{document}|,
  before the hook management existed. It is set to \cs{@empty}
  and \cs{AtBeginDocument} no longer adds to it; it uses the
  \texttt{begindocument} hook instead. For compatibility, code that
  packages add to \cs{@begindocumenthook} directly (e.g., with
  \cs{g@addto@macro}) in the preamble is still picked up and added to
  \texttt{begindocument} under the label \texttt{legacy}. This support
  will vanish in a future release; use \cs{AtBeginDocument} or
  \cs{AddToHook}.

  At \verb|\begin{document}| the command is made undefined. The kernel
  (\cs{bibliographystyle}, \pkg{utf8ienc}) and many packages therefore
  use \verb|\ifx\@begindocumenthook\@undefined| as a test whether the
  preamble has ended. This use is deprecated as well.

  \todo[inline]{The kernel should stop using \cs{@begindocumenthook} as
    a test for \enquote{still in the preamble} (\cs{bibliographystyle}
    in \texttt{ltbibl}, two places in \texttt{utf8ienc}) and use a
    dedicated test instead.}
\end{function}

  hypdestopt, jmlrbook, metastr}

  \texttt{enddocument} hook instead. For compatibility, code that packages
  add to \cs{@enddocumenthook} directly in the preamble is still picked
  up and added to \texttt{enddocument} under the label \texttt{legacy}.
  Code added after \verb|\begin{document}| is silently lost. This support
  will vanish in a future release; use \cs{AtEndDocument} or
  \cs{AddToHook}.
\end{function}
